properties.statement:
THE 2026-08-08 SEAT-LIVENESS FIX LANDED ON THE TRANSPORT THAT DID NOT NEED IT AND MISSED THE ONE THAT REPORTED IT: A SEAT RETURNED BY THE `mint_seat` TOOL IS NEVER REGISTERED, SO `gone` IS STILL UNREACHABLE FOR IT — AND THE TOOL NOW PROMISES OTHERWISE IN ITS OWN OUTPUT. Follows fact:defect-claim-liveness-is-the-servers-pid-not-the-sessions (w-613d836b, 2026-08-07), which #100 answered with a SeatRegistry: register on attach, remove on drop, so a departed session reads `gone` instead of borrowing the daemon's pid. That mechanism WORKS. Nothing on the served path populates it. MEASURED HERE 2026-08-08 against v0.25.0 source, by running the tool handler and probing liveness directly:
    tool-minted seat   before=Live   after release_seat=Live    <- gone unreachable
    registered seat                  after release_seat=Gone    <- the fix, on a path nothing calls
THE MECHANISM, three links, each directly readable: (1) the registry is populated ONLY by `identity::SeatLease::attach()`; (2) the only callers are service.rs wrap_at and share, which build the service's OWN seat; (3) `seat_for_claim` uses that seat ONLY when the caller OMITS `seat`, and `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/claims_tools.rs:114` mints the tool's seat with bare `identity::mint_seat()` and never registers it. So the registry answers for the session-held seat, and `dec:stateless-seat-handle` REFUSES the omit path on the sessionless transport — which is precisely where a caller must pass a tool-minted seat, and precisely the deployment (`--shared`) the original defect was reported from. WORSE THAN A MISS, AN OVERCLAIM: the same change added `liveness_is_this_session` to mint_seat's output — 'Your claims read `live` while you are attached and `gone` once you are not — including if this session crashes rather than exits cleanly.' That is FALSE for the seat that tool returns. The field it replaced said the opposite and WAS TRUE. A correct caveat was traded for an incorrect promise, which is strictly worse than the original defect: a reader who believed the old text was right to distrust liveness, and a reader who believes the new text is wrong to trust it. WHY THE CHECK DID NOT CATCH IT, AND THE PRECEDENT THAT SAYS WHAT TO DO: `ver:claim-liveness` is `passing` and its own name states its scope — 'Proven end to end over stdio with a genuinely exited server process'. Stdio is the one transport where the caller may omit `seat` and get the registered lease, so the check proves the fixed path and never touches the broken one. crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/ contains NO liveness test at all; the regression test lives in reflow2-core/tests/claims.rs and calls `register_seat` BY HAND, supplying the very step the server omits. That is what made a real fix look proven. This project has already split a check for exactly this reason — ver:a-session-cannot-name-another-design was carved out of ver:sessions-cannot-cross-designs on 2026-08-07 because a green check standing for an untested clause is worse than an absent one. Same remedy applies. REPORTED INDEPENDENTLY THE SAME DAY by dev_storyflow w-aa0607ff (api-boss fleet, ~18:12 EDT), who measured two different sessions' seats sharing pid 3840196 = the --serve-shared process, and correctly concluded `gone` can never fire. They were running 0.24.0 (their export stamp), so they had not seen #100; the finding stands on v0.25.0 regardless, which is the part worth knowing. THEIR GENERALISATION IS THE MOST VALUABLE LINE IN THE REPORT AND SHOULD BE RUN AS A SWEEP: `--shared` 'turned a session-local metric into a shared-state one WITHOUT CHANGING ITS INTERFACE' was already ratified about loop_status counts, and nobody re-audited the other tools whose meaning --shared silently changed. The greppable question: WHICH OUTPUTS DESCRIBE A SESSION BUT ARE COMPUTED FROM SOMETHING THE SERVER OWNS? FIX SHAPE: register the seat the `mint_seat` tool hands out (it is the seat that will be carried), or — since nothing ties that seat to a client connection — make the field say what it can actually observe, per their proposal: `liveness: "unknown (shared server - cannot observe client sessions)"`. A field that cannot produce its negative value must not present its positive one as information. Either way the mint_seat advisory must stop asserting the behaviour it does not have.
